rationale: The candidate reads as one coherent massing idea: a rectilinear perimeter slab wrapped around a central court, then lifted to create a legible threshold. In all four views the object stays consistent, without obvious solid collisions or view-dependent contradictions. The green parcel is respected, and the dominant figure is not just box-filling; it responds with an internal void and a controlled outer perimeter. The blue access edge is acknowledged by the open court/undercut side, though the response is still somewhat muted and could be clearer as a public-facing seam. Program-wise, the mass plausibly supports neighborhood living / mixed-use through a compact street edge, one primary public void, and calm upper massing. It is not overly sculptural, and it avoids the wrong-typology problem. The silhouette is coherent but fairly simple; the stepped/lifted section is present without becoming a full terraced landform. Overall this is a successful early-stage massing with a solid anchor and understandable hierarchy, but it could better articulate the access side and section.
